claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is single-phase BCC.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a dendritic microstructure.
The alloy has approximately 800 MPa yield strength at lower temperature.
The alloy sustains approximately 40% strain at lower temperature.
At 1273 K, the alloy has approximately 330 MPa yield strength.
At 1273 K and 30% strain, the alloy has approximately 423 MPa compressive strength.
Y2O3 nanoparticles are stable at the proposed elevated temperature.
Powder metallurgy and controlled consolidation can introduce approximately 1–2 wt% oxide nanoparticles into TiVNbTa.
The processing will produce a uniform dispersion of oxide nanoparticles within grains.
The processing will produce oxide nanoparticles at grain boundaries.
Oxide nanoparticle dispersoids will obstruct dislocation motion.
Oxide nanoparticle dispersoids will inhibit grain-boundary sliding.
Obstructing dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will retard creep at elevated temperature.
The oxide dispersion will help maintain structural integrity at elevated temperature.
The treated alloy will retain yield strength above 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The treated alloy will exceed 423 MPa compressive strength at 1273 K under a similar deformation level.
The expected improvement applies up to 1273 K and at approximately 30–40% plastic strain when oxidation is controlled.
The strengthening effect is limited to the single-phase BCC, dendritic state of TiVNbTa.

contradictions.description: The intervention describes the oxide amount as a 'volume fraction' but quantifies it in wt%; weight percent and volume fraction are distinct measures.

The boundary limits the effect to a single-phase state, while the intervention deliberately introduces a dispersed oxide phase. The BCC matrix could remain single-phase, but the resulting oxide-dispersion-strengthened material is not literally a single-phase material.
